question_stem:
A thin slice of conducting material is placed normal to a uniform magnetic field, as shown in Fig. 8.1.

{{figure:figure_8_1}}

The magnetic field is normal to face CDEF and to face PQRS.

The current $I$ in the slice is normal to the faces CDQP and FERS.

A potential difference, the Hall voltage $V_{\text{H}}$, is developed across the slice.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: State the faces between which the Hall voltage $V_{\text{H}}$ is developed.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Explain why a constant voltage $V_{\text{H}}$ is developed between the faces you have named in (i).

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Two slices have similar dimensions. One slice is made of a metal and the other slice is made of a semiconductor material.

For the same values of magnetic flux density and current, state which slice, if either, will give rise to the larger Hall voltage. Explain your reasoning.
